ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 70:30 ratio of high-intensity white/cream pixels to low-intensity black/dark-brown pixels across the visible ventral fluke surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant high-intensity white central lobes. Significant low-intensity brownish-yellow contiguous blobs (diatom film) covering the central-inner regions of both lobes. Black high-contrast contiguous banding follows the trailing edge and extends into the lateral margins.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: V-shaped central depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 42 degrees; depth extends approximately 12% into the fluke vertical axis.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration profile. Continuous peaks and valleys with pixel amplitudes ranging from 5 to 15 pixels; larger irregular excisions visible on the inner-left and inner-right trailing edge quadrants.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly convex curve from the median notch extending to 85% of lobe width, transitioning to a terminal concavity at the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, high-contrast clusters of circular pinkish-white and grey pixel groupings (barnacles) localized at the extreme distal tips of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Detection of multiple thin, dark-grey linear pixel disruptions; notably a cluster of vertical marks on the lower-left ventral quadrant and isolated horizontal marks on the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Massive localized parasitic colonization (Coronula diadema/Conchoderma auritum) at the fluke tips; extensive brownish surface discoloration consistent with biological film accumulation.
other_distinctive_markers: The trailing edge silhouette is significantly modified at the tips by protruding biological masses that break the continuous linear boundary of the fluke skin.
